problems: Caption says many flash at once 'near the end', but the densest flashing is in storyboard frames 9-11 (about 4-5.5 s of 7.5 s). The last frames (14-16) are as sparse as the start, so the film ends on the scattered state, not on the shared flash.

The shared flash does not read as one beat. Even in frames 9-11 the dots are still scattered and uneven, and frame 2 has a similar burst early on. A viewer cannot see fireflies on separate clocks coming together.

The fireflies are tiny pure-white dots, the same size and colour as the stars in the sky (at-25, at-50 and at-75 all show this). Against the sky and the distant village they cannot be told apart from stars, and they look more like snow or dust than fireflies.

The flashes light nothing. No grass, path, tree trunk or fence brightens near a bright dot, even the large close ones in at-75 (left foreground, bottom right), so they look pasted on, not glowing in the scene.
It doesn't look like dusk. The sky is a bright blue-grey and the ground, path and fence are lit in warm sunlight with hard shadows, yet stars fill the sky. The light contradicts itself.
A fence plank next to the stone lantern leans over during the film (upright in at-25, tilted in at-75 and storyboard frames 13-15). Nothing visible pushes it.
The film's file name, 'fireflies-learn-my-beat', promises fireflies following someone's beat. Nothing in the film shows a beat or anyone setting one.
posts.critique: The fixed shot of the village at dusk is pleasant, but the white dots are lost among the stars, and the 'many flash at once' moment comes in the middle, is weak and fades out before the end. The caption claims a synchronisation the film doesn't clearly show, and the sunlit lighting under a starry sky makes the dusk unconvincing.
